item.title: Trukai supports Morobe show participants
item.description: Trukai Industries is supporting cultural groups, horse riders, bikers, security guards and other participants at this weekend’s Morobe Provincial Agricultural Show through its continued sponsorship of the annual event. The company’s latest contribution includes 200 bags of rice, 200 bags of flour and merchandise, following an earlier K133,100 cheque presentation to the Morobe Show Committee.
item.content:encoded:
Trukai Industries is supporting cultural groups, horse riders, bikers, security guards and other participants at this weekend’s Morobe Provincial Agricultural Show through its continued sponsorship of the annual event.

The company’s latest contribution includes 200 bags of rice, 200 bags of flour and merchandise, following an earlier K133,100 cheque presentation to the Morobe Show Committee.

Trukai National Sales and Marketing Manager Heral Buksh said the company had maintained its partnership with the show for 40 years and thanked the committee for recognising its continued support.

“This is a partnership we have carried for the last 40 years. We thank the committee for recognising us,” Buksh said.

Trukai has been recognised as Reserve Grand Champion Sponsor this year, after receiving Blue Ribbon Champion Sponsor recognition last year.

The Morobe Provincial Agricultural Show brings together farmers, agricultural exhibitors, businesses and communities to showcase agricultural products, livestock and cultural traditions.

The show will be held at the Lae Showgrounds on October 24 and 25.

item.title: NiuPay appoints Vontis Paska to lead Northern Region operations
item.description: NiuPay Limited has appointed Vontis Paska as General Manager for the Northern Region, strengthening its presence in Lae as the company expands its digital services across Morobe and other parts of Papua New Guinea. Paska will take up the role on November 2, 2026, and lead NiuPay’s permanent Lae office, which the company announced at a Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry business breakfast on Sept
item.content:encoded:
NiuPay Limited has appointed Vontis Paska as General Manager for the Northern Region, strengthening its presence in Lae as the company expands its digital services across Morobe and other parts of Papua New Guinea.

Paska will take up the role on November 2, 2026, and lead NiuPay’s permanent Lae office, which the company announced at a Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry business breakfast on September 28.

He will serve as the main contact for the Lae City Authority, users of its ServiceLink platform and organisations across Morobe and the wider Northern Region, supported by a locally recruited team.

Paska has worked with the Lae City Authority on ServiceLink, an online platform for land tax payments and other municipal services, since the project began.

He has also worked with the Department of Lands and Physical Planning on its ‘e Lands’ and ‘go Lands’ land administration platforms and the delivery of Papua New Guinea’s first digital strata titles.

Before joining NiuPay in 2023, Paska worked at the Internal Revenue Commission, where he helped deliver ‘My IRC’, the country’s first online tax payment system, in 2021.

He has more than 10 years of experience across the public service and private sector and serves as an executive board member of the PNG ICT Cluster.

NiuPay Chief Operating Officer Trevor Manokore said Paska’s experience working with the Lae City Authority made him well suited to lead the company’s regional operations.

“Vontis has worked alongside Lae City Authority from the start, and he has earned the trust.” Manokore said.

item.title: Grade 12 attack reveals ongoing attacks to school
item.description: The recent attack on grade 12 students and invigilators of Bishop Leo Secondary in Wewak has revealed that the school and teachers had been enduring continuous attacks by thieves from neighboring communities over the years. A school staff told NBC News that stealing in teachers' residence happens frequently.
item.content:encoded:
The recent attack on grade 12 students and invigilators of Bishop Leo Secondary in Wewak has revealed that the school and teachers had been enduring continuous attacks by thieves from neighboring communities over the years.

A school staff told NBC News that stealing in teachers' residence happens frequently.

Earlier this year, the school's storeroom was vandalized with school uniforms and merchandise stolen and destroyed.

Give the severity of the recent attack where students' exam was disrupted and students were robbed; police and community leaders are expected to step up.

Meanwhile, the suspects involved in Friday's incident that affected Grade 12 students at Bishop Leo Secondary School, will be handed over police today.

A community leader, Tednol Wally told NBC News that he will be bringing in the 20 who surrendered, to police today at 3pm.

Wali is the ward councilor for Nuigo, one of the neighboring communities of Bishop Leo Secondary School.

item.title: Low water at Yonki cuts power supply
item.description: Water storage at Yonki Dam in Eastern Highlands Province has fallen to 35.46 per cent of its full capacity, reducing hydroelectricity generation and forcing PNG Power Limited to continue load shedding across Lae, Madang and the Highlands. item.content:encoded:
Water storage at Yonki Dam in Eastern Highlands Province has fallen to 35.46 per cent of its full capacity, reducing hydroelectricity generation and forcing PNG Power Limited to continue load shedding across Lae, Madang and the Highlands.

PNG Power chief executive officer, Paul Bayly said prolonged dry weather associated with El Niño had significantly reduced water inflows into the dam, which supplies water for electricity generation at Yonki Toe and Ramu hydro power stations.

As of October 20, 2026, the dam’s available water storage for power generation had dropped to 35.46 per cent of full capacity.

The reduced water supply has affected electricity generation at a time when customers across the Ramu grid require about 90 megawatts during peak demand.

Yonki hydro generation is currently producing about 50 megawatts on a normal day, leaving a shortfall of approximately 40 megawatts.

The Ramu grid supplies electricity to Lae, Madang, Mount Hagen, Jiwaka, Goroka and Simbu.

PNG Power said the current power interruptions were caused by insufficient generation resulting from the reduced water inflows, rather than equipment failure or damage to the electricity network.

Despite rainfall in Lae, the situation at Yonki Dam remains a concern because the dam’s catchment continues to experience prolonged dry weather.

PNG Power said it was carefully managing water releases to prevent storage from falling below 10 per cent of full capacity, the minimum safe operating level needed to protect generating equipment and sustain power supply.

The utility warned that running the dam down too quickly could lead to a longer and more severe electricity shortage later.

Load shedding is therefore being used to manage the available generation and maintain stability across the Ramu grid.

PNG Power expects the interruptions to continue for the remainder of 2026 and into the next wet season, which the National Weather Service forecasts to begin in the second quarter of 2027.

The company is assessing temporary power generation options to support the grid during the dry period, while longer-term plans include additional hydro, solar and gas-fired generation to reduce reliance on Yonki Dam.

PNG Power has apologised to customers affected by the ongoing interruptions and said the return to normal supply would depend largely on rainfall and the recovery of water levels at Yonki Dam.

item.title: MULLG to support Madang Technical College
item.description: Madang's Town Mayor, Ishmael Yama, has confirmed that, Madang Urban Local Level Government (MULLG) will consider giving some financial assistance to the Madang Technical College annually to help with small projects. Yama paid a courtesy visit to the college last Friday to show MULLG's support to the school and applauded Governor Ramsey Pariwa's recent assistance of K500, 000 to prepares itself tow
item.content:encoded:
Madang's Town Mayor, Ishmael Yama, has confirmed that, Madang Urban Local Level Government (MULLG) will consider giving some financial assistance to the Madang Technical College annually to help with small projects.

Yama paid a courtesy visit to the college last Friday to show MULLG's support to the school and applauded Governor Ramsey Pariwa's recent assistance of K500, 000 to prepares itself towards becoming a Polytechnical institute in the future.

The Town Mayor said that he was privileged to be at the college and to have met with the teachers and student leaders after Governor Pariwa's visit on October 1.

In a brief meeting with the college principal, staff, and student leaders; Yama expressed his sincere apology for not being able to be at the college during the governor's visit, adding he was in Port Moresby following up on some project submissions for MULLG.

Yama explained that MULLG did not capture school assistance in this year's budget but will make sure it is included in next year's budget.

"We don’t have any financial support for educational institutions this year in our budget, but going forward, I would like to make a commitment and pledge MULLG's support to Madang Technical College. At this point in time, I can't make any commitments because there is nothing in our budget.

"But from next year onwards, we will try to squeeze in some funding assistance for the college.

"I think I have sighted a request from the college in my office, but at this point in time, we cannot entertain it because there is nothing in the budget for education. We will include it in next year's budget," Yama said.

The mayor, meanwhile; also indicated his government's willingness to engage students from Madang Technical College in MULLG's infrastructure construction and maintenance around town.

Yama said that he was impressed with the work that students from the Building and Construction, Plumbing and Sheet Metal, Furniture and Cabinet Making, plus Painting and Sign Writing departments are doing during their On- The- Job Trainings.

He stated, "MULLG will also look at engaging some of the students from this college to help with its infrastructure maintenance and construction around town. Instead of engaging expensive contractors to construct new buildings or even maintain rundown infrastructures, why don't we engage the students. It is part of their training."

The students usually do their OJT attachments for four weeks during their second year of studies.

Some of their recent attachments were with Madang Country Club, Globe Manufacturing Company, GMI Properties, JR Company, and others.

The Madang Government's assistance to the college on October 1 was to help with infrastructure maintenance and development as the institute begins discussions on the possibility of upgrading its status to a polytechnical college for the Momase Region in the near future.

item.title: ICCC warns PMV operators
item.description: PMV owners and operators who overcharge passengers under the newly approved fares have been warned that they will face hefty fines. Independent Consumer and Competition Commission [ICCC] Commissioner Roy Daggy issued the warning on NBC’s Let’s Talk About It program in Port Moresby today.
item.content:encoded:
PMV owners and operators who overcharge passengers under the newly approved fares have been warned that they will face hefty fines.

Independent Consumer and Competition Commission [ICCC] Commissioner Roy Daggy issued the warning on NBC’s Let’s Talk About It program in Port Moresby today.

The new PMV fares took effect Monday morning, with passengers paying a fare of K2 for all urban routes, regardless of distance travelled, including short trips such as from Foodland bus stop to 4-Mile bus stop.

Daggy says the ICCC will work closely with relevant authorities to ensure PMV and taxi operators comply with the approved fares.

Daggy emphasised that operators who fail to comply and overcharge passengers will face hefty fines.

Meanwhile, the ICCC will work with relevant authorities to ensure PMVs and taxis comply with the approved fares.

item.title: ACP Dalla calls for accountability and better management
item.description: Accountability and management were the main focus of the Highlands Eastern End Police Command's third-quarter meeting in Mt Hagen last week. Assistant Commissioner of Police Clement Dalla says police commanders must take responsibility for their duties and ensure that issues raised during previous meetings are properly addressed.
item.content:encoded:
Accountability and management were the main focus of the Highlands Eastern End Police Command's third-quarter meeting in Mt Hagen last week.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Clement Dalla says police commanders must take responsibility for their duties and ensure that issues raised during previous meetings are properly addressed.

Speaking at the meeting held at Airport Motel, ACP Dalla said the quarterly gatherings were important for reviewing police operations, identifying challenges and finding ways to improve service delivery.

He said the meeting brought together Provincial Police Commanders and other senior officers responsible for policing in Western Highlands, Jiwaka and Simbu provinces.

“Our agenda is normally centred around issues that affect our operations, the challenges we face and what we can do to improve on them.

“Much of the discussion during this one day third quarter meet was around accountability and management because this is a high-level management meeting for the command and that whatever items, issues at the PPCs closure must be reported back to the command with accountability and prudent management,” ACP Dalla said.

Dalla said police commanders discussed several issues affecting their daily operations, including logistics, funding and manpower shortages.

He stressed these challenges were common across government departments, but police must continue finding ways to work around them to ensure people receive the security and protection they need.

The meeting also reviewed action points carried forward from the previous two quarterly meetings.

ACP Dalla added some of the issues raised earlier had yet to be addressed, prompting him to urge provincial commanders to explain the progress they had made.

“Some of the agenda items were carried forward from our previous two quarterly meetings. Most of them were action items that had not been acted on.

“I urged the PPCs to go through each of these items and tell us exactly what they have done so far to address the issues raised of which the three PPCs of Simbu, Jiwaka, and Western Highlands have put forward." Dalla said.

He also said the quarterly meetings were not only about discussing problems but also about ensuring that decisions made by the command led to action.

The meetings cover both operational performance and administrative requirements, with the aim of improving the overall management of police services across the three provinces.

The Highlands Eastern End Police Divisional Commander added that the command would continue using these meetings to assess its performance, address outstanding issues and improve the way police services are delivered.

For the Highlands Eastern End Command, stronger accountability and management remain important in overcoming operational challenges and ensuring police officers can effectively carry out their duties.

item.title: Eastern Highlands leaders pay tribute to late Daulo MP
item.description: Mourners dressed in black, with mud smeared on their faces, gathered at Goroka Airport on Friday evening to welcome the body of late Daulo Member of Parliament (MP) Ekime Gorosahu, as Eastern Highlands Province paid its final respects to one of its leaders. Obura-Wonenara MP and Minister for Agriculture John Boito, alongside Henganofi MP and senior statesman Robert Atiyafa, paid tribute to Gorosah
item.content:encoded:
Mourners dressed in black, with mud smeared on their faces, gathered at Goroka Airport on Friday evening to welcome the body of late Daulo Member of Parliament (MP) Ekime Gorosahu, as Eastern Highlands Province paid its final respects to one of its leaders.

Obura-Wonenara MP and Minister for Agriculture John Boito, alongside Henganofi MP and senior statesman Robert Atiyafa, paid tribute to Gorosahu’s dedication to his people.

During the funeral eulogy, Boito recalled a story shared by Gorosahu’s son about his father’s concern for the people of Daulo, even during illness.

“In 2019, while seriously ill, Gorosahu said, ‘If I die today, I will not worry about anything but my people in Daulo,’” Boito recounted.

He also highlighted Gorosahu’s commitment to his duties, saying he continued carrying work documents even while confined to a wheelchair.

“Even while confined to a wheelchair, he remained dedicated to his duties, continuing to carry his work documents and serve the people of Daulo,” Boito said.

Meanwhile, Atiyafa urged Eastern Highlands residents to respect and appreciate their leaders while they are alive, rather than wait until their passing to recognise their worth.

“Let us appreciate our leaders while they are alive instead of accusing them or speaking hurtful words against them,” Atiyafa said.

Other Provincial Executive Council members, including Governor Simon Sia, Okapa MP Sonoma Saki and local-level government presidents, also paid their tribute to Gorosahu.

The late Gorosahu’s casket was escorted to the Provincial Miruso House of Assembly, where it was formally handed over by the National Parliament to the Provincial Executive Council and then to Daulo District representatives.

The Daulo District Development Authority will hold a formal ceremony later this week to hand over the casket to Gorosahu’s immediate family.
